steps.description: Filter genes with edgeR::filterByExpr (group = condition), then TMM-normalize (calcNormFactors) and run limma-voom with a fixed-effects design ~condition, with control set as the reference level explicitly. plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE: significance and effect size
plan.analytical_narrative: 60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 120 samples after excluding any non-sample metadata column). At n=60 per group the knowledge base flags that count-based negative-binomial models (DESeq2/edgeR exact/GLM) inflate false positives in population cohorts because sample-to-sample variance departs from the NB assumption even under permuted labels — so the grounded procedure is limma-voom with TMM normalization and precision weights, cross-checked against a non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum test as a robustness control. Because the research question explicitly separates 'significant' from 'large enough to matter', every differential step reports both the adjusted p-value (BH, alpha=0.05) and the shrunken effect size (log2FC via apeglm/ashr where applicable), and calls out genes that are significant but sub-threshold in effect size versus genes that clear both bars. Enrichment runs on the full ranked gene list (moderated t-statistic) with camera (accounts for inter-gene correlation, appropriate at this sample size) and fgsea preranked as a second method, against MSigDB Hallmark first and Reactome as follow-up, both reference sets confirmed present in this environment. All steps are grounded in the Inflexa full_plan procedure returned for this exact situation (n=60/60, single batch, salmon counts, human); qc, filtering, normalization, model design, DE testing, shrinkage, multiple testing and enrichment steps carry the retrieved claim IDs and template names.
